input: Write a complaint letter to my landlord

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific issue(s) being complained about entirely shape the content and focus of the letter — a noise complaint is structured very differently from a repair dispute or an illegal fee.
Whether prior complaints have already been made (verbally or in writing) determines whether this is a first notice or an escalation, which changes the tone and legal framing significantly.
Knowing whether the letter goes to a private individual landlord, a property management company, or a letting agency affects the salutation, formality level, and who holds legal responsibility.

A deadline or urgency level (e.g., a health/safety hazard vs. a minor inconvenience) determines whether the letter demands a response within a specific timeframe and how assertive the language should be.
The desired tone — firmly assertive, diplomatic, or legally threatening — directly controls word choice and overall framing of the letter.
The specific outcome the user wants (repair completed, refund issued, behaviour stopped) must be stated clearly in the letter as a call to action, so knowing this upfront is essential.
Whether the letter will be sent by email, printed post, or recorded delivery affects formatting, sign-off conventions, and whether a read-receipt or proof-of-delivery note should be included.

gold.taskTitle: Write a complaint letter to your landlord
gold.taskDescription: Draft a formal complaint letter addressed to the user's landlord about one or more unresolved issues with their rental property.

questions.title: What specific issue are you complaining about?
questions.description: Identify the exact problem — e.g., unrepaired maintenance, mould, withheld deposit, noise, unlawful entry — so the letter stays focused and factual.

questions.title: Have you already raised this with your landlord before?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a first complaint or a follow-up escalation, which changes the tone and any references to prior communication.

questions.title: Who exactly is the letter addressed to?
questions.description: Clarify whether the recipient is a private landlord, a property management company, or a letting agency, to set the correct salutation and legal framing.

questions.title: How urgent or serious is this issue to you?
questions.description: Establish whether the matter is a health/safety risk or a lower-priority concern, which determines deadlines demanded and assertiveness of language.

questions.title: What tone do you want the letter to strike?
questions.description: Decide between a polite-but-firm approach, a strictly professional tone, or a legally assertive stance to guide word choice throughout.

questions.title: What specific outcome do you want from this letter?
questions.description: Define the desired resolution — repair completed, money refunded, behaviour stopped — so a clear call to action can be included.

questions.title: How will you be sending this letter?
questions.description: Confirm the delivery method — email, printed letter, or recorded post — to apply the correct formatting, sign-off, and any delivery-proof language.
